local.scope: working tree including Unreleased changes; not the published npm artifact

limitations: Source-level capability inventory, not execution or a security review of every line.
Instruction presence, runtime code presence, tests and live verification are distinct.
Covered denotes the same scoped purpose, not universal behavioral parity.
Optional and experimental entries remain differences; they are not silently counted as implemented.
One pinned snapshot cannot guarantee parity with future upstream changes.

groups.title: General engineering workflows
groups.current: Source-aware planning, specifications, implementation, debugging, cleanup, review and verification have maintained methods.
groups.difference: ECC uses different names and some more prescriptive sequences; naming and command counts do not establish quality.
groups.requires: Keep concrete workflow contracts and evidence-based completion; add only a separately identified method gap.
groups.acceptance: Existing method fixtures and live-host samples remain evidence for their tested cases only.

groups.title: Architecture and decision methods
groups.current: Eight architecture workflows and eight decision workflows cover boundaries, contracts, scale, ADRs and revisiting assumptions.
groups.difference: The basic architectural purpose is present; ECC-specific templates are not byte-for-byte equivalents.
groups.requires: Reuse current architecture and decision workflows; preserve concrete source and constraints.
groups.acceptance: A decision record must identify alternatives, evidence, reversible choices and a revisit trigger.

groups.title: Frontend interaction and design methods
groups.current: UI, accessibility, motion, responsiveness, state and visual-diff workflows are present with icon and reduced-motion constraints.
groups.difference: Missing dedicated design-direction, motion-library and product click-path recipes; no bundled design-media pipeline.
groups.requires: Extend conditional guides for motion libraries, click-path audits, design-system extraction and evidence from real browser states.
groups.acceptance: Verify keyboard/focus, reduced motion, page transitions, loading/failure states and widths in a browser; do not equate generated screenshots with shipped UI.

groups.title: React-specific work
groups.current: Eight focused React workflows plus framework rules cover effects, state, forms, async behavior, rendering and hydration.
groups.difference: ECC has additional worked React testing/build/review material; comparable method coverage is not proof of equal example depth.
groups.requires: Audit repository-specific React test/build cases and add missing focused examples, keeping framework-version distinctions.
groups.acceptance: Use discriminating state, cancellation, hydration and interaction tests; profile before claiming render improvements.

groups.title: Vite tooling
groups.current: Eight Vite workflows cover setup, config, HMR, environment, bundles, chunks, assets and upgrades.
groups.difference: No separate missing Vite tool was established at this snapshot; framework combinations are recorded in framework-web.
groups.requires: Maintain installed-version checks and application-specific build evidence.
groups.acceptance: Verify HMR/build behavior in the actual repository rather than counting configuration fields.

groups.title: Backend, deployment and infrastructure depth
groups.current: API/backend, container, deployment, incident and reliability workflows exist.
groups.difference: No dedicated Kubernetes or Flox environment recipes, latency-critical systems method, Uncloud deployment recipe or content-hash-cache example.
groups.requires: Add conditional deployment/environment guides with real prerequisites, rollback and resource bounds; separate optional services from built-in tools.
groups.acceptance: Exercise representative health/rollback, signal/shutdown, retry and environment-reproduction failures on the selected stack.

groups.title: Database core methods
groups.current: Schema, migrations, queries, query plans, indexes, locks, integrity and access have specialized workflows.
groups.difference: Engine-specific recipes are separate depth gaps; generic DB workflows must not be used to declare engine parity.
groups.requires: Retain current core methods and extend only the missing engine guides.
groups.acceptance: Changes must use schema/transaction evidence and representative plan or concurrency checks.

groups.title: Test and regression workflows
groups.current: Unit, integration, E2E, property, regression, flaky, fixture and load methods exist, with proof artifacts and host trials.
groups.difference: Dedicated Windows desktop automation, cross-agent regression recipes and repository-independent benchmark optimization loops are not bundled.
groups.requires: Add platform-specific desktop and benchmark guides only with actual runners and versioned fixtures; retain hypothesis-driven testing.
groups.acceptance: Record platform/browser/host versions, failure cases and limits; avoid arbitrary coverage targets as a substitute for meaningful tests.

groups.title: Security review and scans
groups.current: Technical security methods, a native static configuration scanner, SARIF/JSON/Markdown reports and an explicitly trusted AgentShield bridge exist.
groups.difference: No maintained supply-chain IOC feed/scanner, dedicated authorized bounty workflow, or GateGuard-style pre-edit fact collection. External InsAIts integration is also absent.
groups.requires: Add an advisory-source provenance model and exact package/version/config matching; separate static heuristics, verified exploits and optional model analysis.
groups.acceptance: Test stale/adversarial advisories, exact version matching, redaction and no-execution scans; never report unsupported CVE findings.

groups.title: ML methods and specialized libraries
groups.current: Thirty-two ML workflows, eight LLM workflows and ML profiles cover data, training, evaluation and serving.
groups.difference: Missing dedicated PyTorch build/debug recipes, recommender-system architecture and ML adoption playbook; generic ML breadth is not their implementation.
groups.requires: Add conditional guides for autograd/device/distributed training, retrieval/ranking evaluation, online-offline skew and staged ML adoption.
groups.acceptance: Use small CPU fixtures for library bugs, time/entity splits and ranking metrics; expensive training remains an explicitly requested action.

groups.title: Reviewed learning and memory adaptation
groups.current: Feedback, negative lessons, conditional preferences, versioned overlays, approval, evolution, imports, exports and rollback are implemented.
groups.difference: ECC has confidence-scored instincts, observer processes and skill amendments; our explicit review model intentionally differs from automatic confidence promotion.
groups.requires: Keep learning provenance and approval boundaries; any new automatic promotion needs separate evidence and a deliberate product decision.
groups.acceptance: Test conflicting lessons, rejection persistence, project/user isolation, stale revisions and rollback without restoring rejected behavior.

groups.title: Install, discovery and owned-file lifecycle
groups.current: Guided install, pack/profile selection, bundled cache retention, host adapters, conflict detection, update/doctor/uninstall and workflow discovery exist.
groups.difference: ECC exposes different command names; automatic upstream fetching and additional host support are separately listed.
groups.requires: Preserve current ownership-aware lifecycle rather than duplicating commands merely for name parity.
groups.acceptance: Run isolated install/update/uninstall and package-manager archive checks; preserve unrelated settings and user edits.

groups.title: Goals, handoffs and portable context
groups.current: Persistent goals, checkpoints, scoped vaults, instruction memory and reviewed context transfer already work.
groups.difference: ECC additionally imports foreign session/memory stores; native transcript session browsing and context-graph connectors are distinct gaps.
groups.requires: Keep current continuity formats stable; add foreign import adapters only with scoped consent and explicit provenance.
groups.acceptance: Preserve collisions, reset imported verification and reject secret-bearing or execution-permission transfers.

groups.title: Planning, workers, worktrees and GitHub epics
groups.current: Bounded worker processes, DAG phases, structured results, reviewed apply/undo, plan canvas and GitHub epic coordination are implemented.
groups.difference: ECC has additional PRD/PRP templates, team-building/delegation conventions and cross-provider roles; no equivalent tmux control plane or continuous scheduler exists here.
groups.requires: Add reusable phase templates and review modes on existing workers; separate autonomous schedulers and terminal management as larger features.
groups.acceptance: Test dependency failure, stale acceptance, retry bounds, cancellation, retained dirty worktrees and exact publication recovery.

groups.title: Automated quality gates and hook tuning
groups.current: Toolchain detection, trusted check presets, batched formatting, staged-content checks and before-action guards exist.
groups.difference: Missing named minimal/standard/strict hook profiles, arbitrary per-hook toggles, native repository pre-push enforcement, console/doc/design-specific hook recipes and session investigation gates.
groups.requires: Provide explicit presets and inspectable hook selection; native Git hook installation must be repository-scoped and preserve existing hooks.
groups.acceptance: Exercise hooks from ordinary Git clients as well as agents, partial staging, paths/quoting, failure timeouts and independent toggles.

groups.title: Context, repetition and scope signals
groups.current: Host-reported context metrics, stale-data handling, repetition hashes, scope warnings and a Claude statusline bridge exist.
groups.difference: ECC combines this with cost estimates; we intentionally keep cost accounting distinct from context health.
groups.requires: Preserve known/unknown/stale distinctions; do not synthesize usage numbers from prompt length.
groups.acceptance: Test session isolation, unknown and stale metrics, debounce and actual hook delivery.

groups.title: Cross-host configuration inventory and cleanup
groups.current: Configuration security scans, executable discovery and owned-install doctor exist.
groups.difference: Missing a normalized cross-host MCP/LSP/plugin inventory, duplicate/conflicting servers, orphaned hooks/permissions/caches, skill overlap and reversible cleanup of non-owned configuration.
groups.requires: Build read-only scoped inventories with redaction, then exact reviewable backup/disable/restore operations; age alone must not imply deletion.
groups.acceptance: Test mixed Claude/Codex/OpenCode formats, malformed data, secrets, symlinks, duplicates, user edits and rollback.

groups.title: Skill portfolio maintenance
groups.current: Our activity report tracks selection, delivery, observations and lessons; skill creation has a workflow.
groups.difference: Missing third-party skill stocktaking, duplicate/overlap review, reference freshness, installed-source compliance, per-skill version/provenance dashboard and amendment queues.
groups.requires: Add inventory and provenance plus evidence-linked human review outcomes; distinguish tool completion from successful user outcomes.
groups.acceptance: Test never-used versus unobserved, version changes, conflicting amendments and broken links; no objective quality claim from raw invocation counts.

groups.title: User-authored behavior rules
groups.current: Current hooks and policies are maintained built-in behaviors, with configured command checks.
groups.difference: No Hookify-style authoring/list/configure workflow. ECC documents declarative warn/block rules, but this audit found no Hookify evaluator wired into its shipped hook dispatcher; enforcement must not be assumed from rule files alone.
groups.requires: Create a versioned declarative rule schema with bounded matchers, preview/explain, enable/disable and recovery; avoid arbitrary evaluator code or pathological regex execution.
groups.acceptance: Test event shapes, Boolean conditions, path scope, non-matches, invalid patterns, rule conflicts, latency bounds and safe failure behavior.

groups.title: MCP connection health and recovery
groups.current: The bundled MCP server has protocol/access checks; discovery reports host-supplied capability evidence.
groups.difference: No host-wide MCP preflight reachability state, failure categorization, reconnect/backoff or cross-harness configuration normalization.
groups.requires: Expose status and bounded diagnostics separately from explicit reconnection; endpoint reachability is not authenticated tool availability.
groups.acceptance: Test OAuth expiry, 401/403/429, timeouts, stdio processes, no double execution, secret redaction and backoff.

groups.title: Native session history and lifecycle snapshots
groups.current: Just-vibe run records, task history, checkpoints, handoffs and cross-worktree context export exist.
groups.difference: Missing native Claude/OpenCode/Codex transcript session adapters, aliases/search/pagination, session inspect/branch/export, interruption-side-question contract and model-generated PreCompact summaries.
groups.requires: Create opt-in adapters for user-visible session content, stable IDs/aliases and bounded previews; build explicit pre-compaction capture without reading private model reasoning.
groups.acceptance: Test corrupt/partial/large logs, cross-project isolation, alias collisions, privacy, stale paths and resume without lost active-task constraints.

groups.title: Optional usage accounting and model advice
groups.current: Context capacity and ML/LLM cost-planning workflows exist; no account-spend ledger is maintained.
groups.difference: ECC records cumulative per-session token/cache usage, estimates spend, exports reports and recommends model tiers.
groups.requires: If added, consume actual host usage, deduplicate cumulative snapshots and version pricing; offer advisory model selection separately from automatic switching.
groups.acceptance: Test missing prices, stale rates, snapshots, currencies and multiple sessions; usage and cost must never be presented as output-quality scores.

groups.title: CodeTour artifacts and maintained codemaps
groups.current: Explain, map, architecture mapping and documentation workflows exist.
groups.difference: No dedicated CodeTour .tour generator/validator or codemap freshness/diff tooling.
groups.requires: Add referenced, bounded walkthrough artifacts with reader intent and file/line anchors; track source identities so stale tours are visible.
groups.acceptance: Reject missing paths and invalid lines; test source moves, stale anchors and regeneration without overwriting hand edits.

groups.title: Bounded iterative and continuous work modes
groups.current: Goals and worker DAGs support bounded tasks and explicit retries.
groups.difference: No persistent continuous-PR/RFC loop manager, loop wakeup/transcript inspector, loop design preflight or autonomous runtime that starts later sessions.
groups.requires: Design a resumable loop state machine with progress evidence, timeout/attempt/spend limits and explicit stop/cancel; use host scheduling when available.
groups.acceptance: Test duplicate wakeups, stuck tools, repeated failure, restarts, cancellation and clean shutdown; no infinite default loops.

groups.title: Independent council and adversarial review modes
groups.current: Decision/challenge workflows and independent specialist workers provide building blocks.
groups.difference: No packaged council, multi-model dissent, two-independent-reviewer convergence, generator/evaluator harness or evidence-based self-reflection contract.
groups.requires: Compose explicit independent review briefs, budgets, stopping rules and disagreement reports on existing worker orchestration; label subjective assessment.
groups.acceptance: Verify independent context, genuine disagreement, bounded repair loops and unresolved verdicts; reviewers cannot self-certify success.

groups.title: Terminal and development-service operations
groups.current: Worker subprocesses and worktrees exist but are not a terminal multiplexer or service manager.
groups.difference: No tmux/dmux pane orchestration, terminal opener/operator, detached development-server hooks or PM2 service-config workflow.
groups.requires: Add optional terminal/service adapters with executable discovery, process ownership, preview, stop and restart; never silently install global tools.
groups.acceptance: Test quoting, already-running services, occupied ports, restart recovery, Windows/WSL limitations and cleanup of owned processes only.

groups.title: Sustained post-deploy monitoring and notifications
groups.current: Deployment verification, Vercel runtime/performance checks, browser evidence and operational workflows exist.
groups.difference: No sustained canary watch with interval/duration, staging-production diff, SSE heartbeat checks or cross-platform desktop completion notifications.
groups.requires: Add bounded explicit monitoring with baseline identity, change-only alerts and cancellation; distinguish a one-shot check from a scheduler.
groups.acceptance: Exercise failed assets, wrong content types, SSE inactivity, transient errors, notification opt-in and stop behavior.

groups.title: User-facing harness evaluation and evidence receipts
groups.current: Maintainer behavior/security/host trials and user proof/lab/experiment artifacts are available.
groups.difference: No general cross-agent task-suite CLI, canonical evaluation capsule/replay format, effect-fenced portable receipts or harness configuration promotion registry. ECC gate execution is explicitly unavailable without isolation at this snapshot.
groups.requires: Define immutable input/artifact identities, trusted verifier execution, repeatable fixtures and comparison reports; keep quality judgments and observed outcomes separate.
groups.acceptance: Test artifact tampering, stale evidence, checker access, inconclusive runs and reproducibility; cryptographic hashes are not proof that claimed observations are true.

groups.title: Agent construction and prompt engineering methods
groups.current: LLM prompt/tool/eval/injection workflows and a skill-authoring workflow exist.
groups.difference: Missing specific agent harness construction, introspection audits, MCP server implementation recipes, routing-surface design and reusable prompt-optimization procedures.
groups.requires: Add focused conditional engineering guides with tool contracts, state ownership, retries and evaluation cases; do not add opaque quality scores.
groups.acceptance: Run representative routing failures, invalid tool inputs, error propagation and injected tool-output fixtures.

groups.title: Python and Django/Celery depth
groups.current: Python rules and Django/FastAPI conditional guides exist.
groups.difference: ECC includes larger Python test/pattern examples and a dedicated Celery task/queue/transaction guide; current guides are not complete equivalents.

groups.acceptance: Use version-pinned minimal fixtures for task redelivery, rollback, cancellation, auth and serialization; mark live broker tests separately.

groups.requires: Add framework-aware conditional recipes for transactions, persistence, cancellation, security filters and test environments.
groups.acceptance: Use project wrappers and declared versions; test transaction boundaries, query behavior, coroutine cancellation and auth failures.

groups.title: Laravel and Rails depth

groups.difference: Missing dedicated Laravel patterns, security, tests, verification and plugin discovery, and substantial Rails-specific implementation recipes.
groups.requires: Add conditional framework guides with migrations, policies, ORM scope, jobs, transactions and version-aware testing.
groups.acceptance: Test mass assignment, tenant scoping, queue retries, rollback and mixed-version migrations on representative apps.

groups.title: Mobile and Apple platform depth

groups.difference: Missing Android clean architecture, Compose Multiplatform, HarmonyOS/ArkTS, SwiftUI, actor persistence, Swift 6.2 concurrency, protocol-DI testing, on-device Foundation Models and Liquid Glass recipes.
groups.requires: Add platform/version-specific guides and specialist checks; preserve accessibility, offline and lifecycle semantics.
groups.acceptance: Use supported simulators/devices/toolchains; test lifecycle cancellation, actor isolation, persistence, navigation and accessibility; label device-only limitations.

groups.difference: Missing detailed .NET patterns and C#/F# test/review recipes.

groups.acceptance: Run pinned SDK fixtures for scoped-service misuse, query translation, cancellation and serialization compatibility.

groups.acceptance: Each agent must have a distinct trigger, allowed scope, failure-specific checks, evidence contract and relevant fixtures.

groups.requires: Provide versioned read-only recipe metadata, prerequisites and explicit setup/trust boundaries; credentials stay with the host.
groups.acceptance: Test schema/transport versions and redaction; verify live accounts separately; do not claim installed/authenticated from a recipe.

groups.title: Brand, media, document and design production
groups.current: Frontend and copy workflows exist, and hosts may separately have image/document tools.
groups.difference: No bundled Taste/Tasteforge pipeline, brand-discovery/voice system, Blender or Manim workflow, Remotion/video editing, slides, icon generation, FAL/VideoDB or document conversion/translation pack.
groups.requires: Treat these as optional production packs with real tool dependencies, licensing, asset provenance and preview/verification steps.
groups.acceptance: Validate actual rendered/exported artifacts, editable sources and tool availability; never advertise a host-only skill as just-vibe content.

groups.title: Scientific databases and literature work

groups.acceptance: Verify identifiers, retrieval dates, citation support, retractions and missing data; no fabricated papers or regulatory conclusions.

groups.title: Marketing, content, sales and investing workflows

groups.difference: Missing article/content/crosspost/social publishing, SEO, lead intelligence, marketing campaigns, competitive analysis/reports, investor materials/outreach and social ranking/connection optimization.
groups.requires: Keep an optional business pack separate from engineering defaults; require source support and explicit authority for outbound publication/contact.
groups.acceptance: Verify claims, audience/account, draft previews, exact external side effects and evidence; no autonomous outreach based on inferred intent.

groups.title: Business, logistics, finance and legal operations
groups.current: General data and operations workflows are engineering-focused.
groups.difference: Missing carrier/billing/customs/energy/procurement/inventory/production/returns/quality workflows, email/messages/workspace operations, agreements/e-signatures, research ops and relationship/channel policies.
groups.requires: Create separate optional packs backed by actually available systems; preserve account identity, reviewable writes and domain-specific validation.
groups.acceptance: Use synthetic records and dry-run fixtures; live financial/legal/logistics actions need task-specific authority and source verification.

groups.title: Healthcare software and PHI-specific methods
groups.current: General security/data/ML methods exist but no healthcare-specific pack does.
groups.difference: Missing CDSS, EMR, healthcare evaluation, PHI and HIPAA-specific workflows/reviewer.
groups.requires: Treat as a dedicated domain pack with current authoritative requirements, clinical validation boundaries and explicit data handling.
groups.acceptance: Use synthetic/deidentified fixtures; separate software checks from clinical efficacy and legal compliance judgments.

groups.title: Blockchain, trading and agent payments
groups.current: No wallet/payment or blockchain-specific execution is bundled.
groups.difference: Missing x402 payments, AMM security, EVM decimals, Keccak distinctions, trading-agent security, prediction-market/oracle analysis and AURA reputation adapter.
groups.requires: Keep optional and isolated from engineering defaults, with exact authority and no automatic wallet/payment action.
groups.acceptance: Use local fixtures/test networks; distinguish financial assertions, reputation signals and source-verified protocol invariants.

groups.title: Sponsored and external compute/control bridges
groups.current: No paid compute broker, Nasiko bridge or proprietary analysis service is bundled.
groups.difference: ECC offers Itô compute/baskets bridges and a pinned Nasiko lifecycle bridge; some Itô inference/training guides explicitly describe unavailable backends.
groups.requires: Document optional provider-agnostic integration boundaries before selecting a vendor; never copy remote bootstrap or live RFQ behavior into default setup.
groups.acceptance: Verify the independently installed tool/version, authenticated identity and exact external operation; unavailable services remain unavailable.

groups.title: Standalone Python LLM provider host
groups.current: Just-vibe delegates model execution to existing Claude/Codex hosts.
groups.difference: ECC additionally includes a Python LLM CLI/provider layer for Claude, OpenAI, Ollama, Atlas and AstraFlow, with prompt and tool execution support.
groups.requires: Treat a new host as a separate product decision, including provider auth, streaming, cancellation, tool authority and maintenance.
groups.acceptance: Run provider contract fixtures and opt-in live tests; no reuse of host credentials outside their documented boundaries.

groups.title: ECC2 operator surface, proximity and coordination
groups.current: Local activity reports, plan canvas, workers, DAGs and reviewed worktree application exist.
groups.difference: No unified interactive operator board/TUI, SQLite session daemon, agent proximity/conflict graph, automatic team rebalance, message inbox, heartbeat enforcement or merge queue. ECC2 README labels alpha; source has substantially more features than its short README list.
groups.requires: Design an optional control plane on existing contracts, with explicit process ownership, coordination state, actions and recoverability; do not pretend a static report is equivalent.
groups.acceptance: Test concurrent updates, process crashes, stale PIDs, conflicting edits, queued merges, inaccessible worktrees, cancellation and exact action permissions.

groups.title: Context graph, connectors and foreign migration
groups.current: Scoped lexical vaults and explicit context transfer exist.
groups.difference: Missing entity/relation/observation graph, pin/compact/recall, connector checkpoints for JSONL/Markdown/env sources and Hermes/OpenClaw-style schedules/tools/plugins/memory migration.
groups.requires: Add scoped provenance-aware import adapters and graph semantics only if product needs justify them; exclude credentials and private model reasoning.
groups.acceptance: Test duplicates, interrupted imports, changed sources, secret filtering, retention and graph deletion; graph recall does not imply semantic embeddings.

groups.title: Persistent scheduled and remote work
groups.current: Explicit goals and foreground bounded worker launches exist; scheduling remains a host capability.
groups.difference: ECC2 contains scheduled tasks, run-due processing, remote dispatch queue/server and computer-use request dispatch.
groups.requires: Prefer host scheduling when supported; an owned service needs authenticated transport, opt-in recurring authority, durable deduplication and revocation.
groups.acceptance: Test restart/clock drift, duplicate triggers, revoked authorization, cancellation, request validation and remote isolation.

groups.title: Operator telemetry and platform readiness
groups.current: Activity and health reports expose recorded operational events and evidence.
groups.difference: Missing OpenTelemetry export, combined platform/coordination inventory, observability readiness, numeric risk/budget enforcement and integrated operator status dashboards.
groups.requires: Add structured export and evidence-based readiness; numeric risk/cost measures must be labeled heuristics with inputs and limits.
groups.acceptance: Verify event identity, redaction, delivery failure, missing telemetry and status freshness; no fabricated objective quality scores.

groups.title: Maintainer infrastructure and release automation
groups.current: Release metadata/archive validation, package-manager checks, tests and a website build already exist.
groups.difference: ECC has additional Docker/Windows harness tests, coverage gates, adapter compliance suites, SLSA release workflows, advisory watch, announcement bots and project-specific platform/discussion audits.
groups.requires: Adopt relevant cross-platform and provenance checks separately from product features; do not copy ECC-specific community/announcement machinery.
groups.acceptance: Run actual supported OS/host matrices and verify artifact provenance; blocked CI minutes or skipped tests cannot be labeled passing.

groups.title: Translations, examples and learning material
groups.current: English documentation, generated references, project examples and a website exist.
groups.difference: ECC includes extensive translated docs, language-specific instruction templates and longform/security/setup guides beyond our documentation set.
groups.requires: Prioritize complete maintained English reference and versioned examples, then deliberate localization with source freshness.
groups.acceptance: Check translated links, preserved command semantics, stale versions and working examples; file count is not capability count.

groups.title: Deprecated compatibility surfaces
groups.current: Current reviewed learning and explicit orchestration provide the corresponding purposes.
groups.difference: ECC retains deprecated continuous-learning/autonomous-loops and legacy command/install copies; these are not independent new capabilities to clone.
groups.requires: Record aliases and deprecations in the audit, preserving only compatibility actually needed by just-vibe users.
groups.acceptance: Ensure aliases resolve to canonical methods without duplicating or silently enabling runtime behavior.

groups.title: Additional hosts and host-native tool surfaces
groups.current: Claude/Codex support and ten additional adapter IDs are present; native event integration is narrower than file installation.
groups.difference: ECC has AdaL, CodeBuddy, JoyCode, Kiro, OpenClaw, Pi and Trae surfaces we lack, plus eight OpenCode tool wrappers, Kiro-specific hooks/steering and an initial gitagent export manifest. Its dependency-analyzer wrapper only reads declared packages and leaves outdated/unused analysis unimplemented. Adapter presence does not prove live event parity.
groups.requires: Verify each official host schema and capability first, then add owned-file/event adapters and focused tool wrappers only with explicit support levels.
groups.acceptance: Test install/update/uninstall, foreign settings, event delivery, permissions and installed SDKs; record live host/OS coverage separately.

groups.title: Local graphical catalog browsers
groups.current: Our website has generated searchable command/profile catalogs and the CLI provides workflow discovery.
groups.difference: ECC also has local browser and Python/Tkinter catalog applications. These are separate from its ECC2 operator control pane; our public website is not an installed desktop catalog manager.
groups.requires: If local/offline GUI management is wanted, reuse canonical catalog data and expose installation actions through reviewed ownership-aware contracts.
groups.acceptance: Test offline navigation/search, stale catalog versions, safe local origins and explicit installation actions.

groups.title: Upstream update orchestration
groups.current: Package installation and owned-file updates exist.
groups.difference: No updater that checks an upstream checkout/release and reinstalls the recorded target selections; ECC has a standalone auto-update command.
groups.requires: Add explicit check/preview/update with pinned version, preserved selections, ownership checks and rollback; do not introduce unrequested background self-update.
groups.acceptance: Test dirty checkout, changed user files, offline registry, incompatible version and recovery.
